Figure 4: Qualitative comparison of localization results on diffusion-generated and traditional manipulation datasets. Existing methods often suffer from missed detections or over-segmentation, whereas the proposed framework produces more complete masks and more precise boundaries across diverse manipulation types.

Figure 3: Overview of the proposed Frequency-Aware Semantic Alignment (FASA) framework. Given an input image, FASA extracts microscopic frequency features via ADB-DCT and macroscopic semantic priors using a frozen CLIP encoder. To explicitly bridge the fundamental micro–macro gap, the proposed framework employs a coherent dual-level alignment strategy. First, the Patch-Level Semantic Alignment (PSA) module learns discriminative real/fake prototypes to establish manipulationaware semantic priors in a shared latent space. Second, the Semantic-Frequency Side Adapter (SF-SA) structurally injects these macroscopic priors into the frequency pathway. Finally, the Prototype-Guided Frequency-Gated Mask Decoder (PG-FMD) dynamically fuses the aligned representations, mitigating semantic over-segmentation and delineating precise manipulation boundaries in the final mask.

Figure 5: Robustness comparison of different methods under Gaussian blur and JPEG compression. The first row reports results on OpenSDI with SD1.5 and SD3, while the second row reports results on the IML benchmark with CASIAv1 and Coverage. Pixel-level F1 is used for evaluation, and higher values indicate better robustness.
